title: Functional proteomics protocol for the identification of interaction partners in Tetrahymena thermophila
protocol: Thaw the cell pellets on ice.
Swirl the cell pellet in room temperature water every few minutes during thawing.
Add 500 μL of protease inhibitors for yeast and 200 μL of 100 mM PMSF to 25 mL of 2× lysis buffer.
Estimate the volume of the thawed cell pellet using a 10 mL pipette.
Mix an equal volume of ice-cold 2× lysis buffer supplemented with protease inhibitors with the cell pellet gently by pipetting up and down.
Adjust the total volume to 15 mL using 1× lysis buffer.
Add 300 μL of 10% NP-40 to achieve a final concentration of 0.2%.
Keep the lysate on ice for 10 min and check for viscosity using a wide-bore P1000 pipette tip.
Add 5 μL of Benzonase to digest the released chromatin, genomic DNA, and RNA resulting in an enhanced solubility of chromatin-associated protein complexes.
Rotate the solution in the cold room using a Nutator (or any other suitable rotator) for 30 min.
Divide the cell lysate into 10 pre-chilled 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, with 1.5 mL lysate in each tube.
Centrifuge the lysate at 16,100 × g for 30 min at 4°C.
Pool the clarified cell lysates by transferring the supernatant to pre-chilled 15 mL Falcon tubes.
Save 50 μL of the cell lysate in a separate Eppendorf tube as input.
Flash freeze the remaining lysate in liquid nitrogen immediately, and store at -80°C.
Take out M2 agarose beads and slowly warm them on ice for 10 min.
Gently rotate the bead slurry in your hand to mix.
Transfer 100 μL of anti-FLAG M2 agarose slurry (50 μL packed beads) to a pre-chilled 15 mL Falcon tube per purification.
Wash the beads with 10 mL ice-cold 1× lysis buffer by gently resuspending.
Centrifuge at 960 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Repeat washing step three times.
Resuspend the beads in 50 μL of 1× lysis buffer (final volume will be 100 μL).
Transfer pooled supernatant from step 11 to the Falcon tube containing M2 agarose beads.
Incubate for 2 h at 4°C with end-to-end rotation.
Transfer 100 μL protein G Dynabeads per purification to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Separate Dynabeads using a magnetic rack (~15–30 s).
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 1 mL 1× lysis buffer, put back on the magnetic rack, and remove the supernatant again.
Repeat this step 3 times.
Finally resuspend the Dynabeads in 100 μL 1× lysis buffer.
Add 5 μg of anti-FLAG antibody to 100 μL of protein G Dynabeads.
Rotate at room temperature (~22°C) for 1 h or overnight at 4°C.
After incubation, magnetically separate the beads.
Remove the supernatant and wash 3 times with 1 mL 1× lysis buffer.
Resuspend in 100 μL 1× lysis buffer.
Transfer to the pooled supernatant from step 11.
Incubate at 4°C with end-to-end rotation for 2–4 h.
Wash 100 μL M2 magnetic beads 3 times with 1× lysis buffer.
Resuspend in 100 μL 1× lysis buffer.
Add to the pooled supernatant from step 11.
Incubate at 4°C with end-to-end rotation.
Cut the end of the pipette tip using a sterile razor blade prior to handling agarose beads.
Resuspend M2-agarose beads in 15 mL IPP300 and rotate for 5 minutes in the cold room.
Centrifuge the mixture for 2 minutes at 960 × g.
Wash the beads twice with 15 mL IPP100-NP-40 buffer.
Wash the beads twice more with 15 mL IPP100 without NP-40.
Resuspend M2-agarose beads in 750 μL of CaCl2/Tris solution and transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 2,700 × g at room temperature (~22°C).
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 500 μL of 0.5 M NH4OH and rotate for 20 minutes at room temperature (~22°C).
Centrifuge for 2 minutes at room temperature at 2,700 × g.
Transfer the supernatant to a new pre-chilled 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Transfer 50 μL of the supernatant to a separate pre-chilled 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for Western blotting analysis.
Flash freeze all samples in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C until further use.
Add 1× Laemmli buffer to the beads after washing steps if elution is done using Laemmli buffer.
Heat at 95°C using a heat block or boiling water for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant, which can be directly used for SDS-PAGE and associated Western blotting.
Load input and affinity purified fractions in duplicates on a 10% SDS-PAGE gel.
Electrophorese the gel according to manufacturer’s instructions or other established protocols.
Transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose or PVDF membrane according to manufacturer’s instructions or other established protocols.
Use anti-FLAG antibody at a dilution of 1:5,000 for immunoblot analysis.
Speedvac purified samples to dryness with no heat.
Resuspend dried material in 100 μL of freshly prepared 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate pH 8.0.
Add 0.75 μg of proteomic grade dimethylated trypsin resuspended in 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0 at a concentration of 0.1 μg/μL.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for ~15 hours with gentle lateral mixing.
Add an extra 0.25 μg of proteomic grade dimethylated trypsin and incubate for an additional ~3 hours at 37°C with gentle lateral mixing.
Speedvac the purified samples to dryness with no heat.
Clean the dried desalted peptides using C18 Stage-Tip prior to mass spectrometry data acquisition.
Store the cleaned samples at -80°C until data acquisition.
